newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cabinet met to discuss budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy cabinet met to discuss budget.

text.p: The Italian cabinet discussed its controversial 1997 budget at a meeting on Tuesday but left leaders of parties in the governing centre-left coalition to make a peace overture to the centre-right opposition.

"We discussed the amendments which are before the Senate (upper house)," Transport Minister Claudio Burlando told reporters after the meeting, for which neither Prime Minister Romano Prodi nor Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini were present.
They are attending an OSCE summit in Lisbon.

Asked whether the cabinet had discussed relations with the opposition, which was due to decide on Wednesday whether to boycott the budget vote in the Senate, Burlando said: "It will be up to the (ruling) majority to make a proposal."

Opposition party leaders in the Senate said on Monday they saw some room for progress on the budget after the government coalition offered greater clarification and some flexibility on special policy-setting powers it wants to award itself.
Those powers, which the government wanted initially to extend to a number of areas including tax measures, would save it from having to keep going back to parliament for approval.
Burlando said the cabinet had discussed a range of possibilities but said it would be up to parliamentary party leaders to take a decision.
The centre-right boycotted a vote in the lower Chamber of Deputies on the 1997 budget, which aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($40.7 billion) off next year's projected deficit.

The package, currently before the Senate budget commission, is due to go to the full upper house chamber on December 10. After approval it will be sent back to the Chamber for voting on changes the Senate made. The entire process must be completed by the end of the month. ($1=1,534 lire)
